parsed.basis: In Sennar, Sudan, a transgender visitor who is discovered faces a national regime that criminalises gender nonconformity itself: Article 152 of the Penal Code prohibits wearing clothing of the opposite sex, applying to presentation regardless of sexual conduct. Same-sex anal sex is also criminalised under Article 148, with penalties up to five years for a first offence, seven for a second and life imprisonment for a third after the death penalty was abolished in 2020. There is no legal gender recognition, gender-affirming care is legally constrained, and state violence including extrajudicial killings and torture, official discrimination and vigilante abuse are documented, with only 17 percent public acceptance of homosexuality in 2019. No region-specific information distinguishes Sennar from the national picture.
